# client.holds()

HoldService takes and releases expiring claims on resources. It is the only
thing in this API that mutates availability.

Two things are deliberately not RPCs: the sweeper that expires lapsed holds
is an internal job, not a call, and conversion to a confirmed booking is
driven by ReservationService, so a hold is never converted by a caller
reaching in here.

There is no UpdateHold. A hold's window and resources are immutable by
construction -- changing either is a different allocation -- so the only
mutations are the two custom methods below.

`client.holds()` calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.HoldService`. Every method is async and returns
`shokki_freebusy::Result`.


## client.holds().create

`async fn create(&self, request: CreateHoldRequest) -> Result<Hold>`

Calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.HoldService.CreateHold` (`POST /v1/holds`).

Takes a hold, allocating concrete resources for the window.

The server chooses which resources are taken from the candidates offered,
under a lock, so two callers racing for the last bay cannot both win.
Send `request_id` to make a retry safe: a retry after a timeout with the
same id returns the original hold rather than taking a second one.

Required: `hold`; unset, the call fails with `Code::InvalidArgument` before it is made.

```rust
use shokki_freebusy::{CreateHoldRequest, Freebusy, Hold};

async fn holds_create(client: &Freebusy) -> shokki_freebusy::Result<()> {
    let request = CreateHoldRequest::new().set_hold(Hold::new());
    let result = client.holds().create(request).await?;
    println!("{result:?}");
    Ok(())
}
```

## client.holds().get

`async fn get(&self, request: GetHoldRequest) -> Result<Hold>`

Calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.HoldService.GetHold` (`GET /v1/{name=holds/*}`).

Retrieves one hold.

Authoritative on expiry: a hold whose expire_time has passed is reported
EXPIRED here even if the sweeper has not yet written that state, so a
caller never sees an ACTIVE hold that no longer reserves anything.

Required: `name`; unset, the call fails with `Code::InvalidArgument` before it is made.

```rust
use shokki_freebusy::{Freebusy, GetHoldRequest};

async fn holds_get(client: &Freebusy) -> shokki_freebusy::Result<()> {
    let request = GetHoldRequest::new().set_name("holds/hold-1");
    let result = client.holds().get(request).await?;
    println!("{result:?}");
    Ok(())
}
```

## client.holds().extend

`async fn extend(&self, request: ExtendHoldRequest) -> Result<Hold>`

Calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.HoldService.ExtendHold` (`POST /v1/{name=holds/*}:extend`).

Pushes a hold's expiry further out.

Measured from now rather than from the current deadline, so repeated calls
cannot accumulate an unbounded reservation. Fails on a hold that is not
ACTIVE -- an expired hold is gone, not extendable.

Required: `name`, `duration`; unset, the call fails with `Code::InvalidArgument` before it is made.

```rust
use shokki_freebusy::{ExtendHoldRequest, Freebusy, wkt};

async fn holds_extend(client: &Freebusy) -> shokki_freebusy::Result<()> {
    let request = ExtendHoldRequest::new()
        .set_name("holds/hold-1")
        .set_duration(wkt::Duration::default());
    let result = client.holds().extend(request).await?;
    println!("{result:?}");
    Ok(())
}
```

## client.holds().release

`async fn release(&self, request: ReleaseHoldRequest) -> Result<Hold>`

Calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.HoldService.ReleaseHold` (`POST /v1/{name=holds/*}:release`).

Gives a hold up before it expires, freeing its resources immediately.

Idempotent: releasing an already-released or expired hold succeeds and
changes nothing, because the caller's intent is already satisfied.

Required: `name`; unset, the call fails with `Code::InvalidArgument` before it is made.

```rust
use shokki_freebusy::{Freebusy, ReleaseHoldRequest};

async fn holds_release(client: &Freebusy) -> shokki_freebusy::Result<()> {
    let request = ReleaseHoldRequest::new().set_name("holds/hold-1");
    let result = client.holds().release(request).await?;
    println!("{result:?}");
    Ok(())
}
```

## client.holds().delete

`async fn delete(&self, request: DeleteHoldRequest) -> Result<()>`

Calls `freebusy.allocation.v1.HoldService.DeleteHold` (`DELETE /v1/{name=holds/*}`).

Deletes a hold record.

Housekeeping for terminal holds, not a way to free resources -- use
ReleaseHold for that. Deleting an ACTIVE hold is rejected, so inventory is
never freed by a path that leaves no audit trail.

Required: `name`; unset, the call fails with `Code::InvalidArgument` before it is made.

```rust
use shokki_freebusy::{DeleteHoldRequest, Freebusy};

async fn holds_delete(client: &Freebusy) -> shokki_freebusy::Result<()> {
    let request = DeleteHoldRequest::new().set_name("holds/hold-1");
    client.holds().delete(request).await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
